overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. The minutes-approval complaint was timely under the three-meetings rule, and the minutes-request complaint was a Public Records Law matter outside its jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to timely respond to a May 6 request for all 2019 meeting minutes, arguing a 10-calendar-day deadline applied.
allegations.key_passage: As this allegation concerns compliance with the Public Records Law, it falls outside the scope of this office

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to approve minutes of meetings held January 7 through May 6 in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: We find that all of the meeting minutes were approved within three public body meetings, with most of the minutes approved at the subsequent meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to timely release meeting minutes; the AG noted the OML does not require release, only timely creation, approval and response to requests.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body release its minutes, but rather that minutes be created and approved in a timely manner

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
